case.title: Weekly use and density spread count each user once
case.custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • About 30 minutes, in one sitting (all four users within the same week, Monday to Sunday).
  • Sign in on the QA branch (sv10043) with the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page. Use a desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide (narrower windows show only the List).
  • Work in one location for the whole case, shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"). To change it: your initials at the top right > Change Location.
  • No Google Analytics access is needed. You read what the Work Orders page sends to Google Analytics in the browser's own developer tools (Chrome or Edge): press F12, click the Network tab, tick Preserve log, and type collect in the filter box. Each analytics message shows as a request named collect; click it and open its Payload tab. Each event in it lists: en (the event name), ep.element_location (the display: list, tech_view or board_view), ep.element_label (the field or the density), ep.setting_source (default = never changed, saved = chosen earlier) and uid (the user). One request can hold several events, one per line.
  • Turn off any ad blocker or privacy extension for this site, and use a new private window for each user, so the messages are not stopped or mixed up.
  • Events to look for: work_orders_display_view (sent each time a display is shown; ep.element_location names it), work_orders_density_load and work_orders_density_change (ep.element_label names the density).

Setup

  1. Settings > Staff: add four new users at this location with a role that has Work Orders View, and finish each invite so they can sign in (e.g. "ZZAUTOTEST F3 Weekly U1" to "U4"). They must be new, so none has used Tech View or Board View before. Do not open either view as them before the steps.
case.custom_steps:
1. For each user below use a new private window with the browser tools open as described in the Preconditions (F12 > Network > Preserve log > filter collect). After each user, write down from the collect requests every work_orders_display_view event (ep.element_location and uid) and the last density event (ep.element_label and uid). Then sign out and close the window.
  2. U1: open Work Orders 5 times (reload the page between visits); each time switch to Board View. Set density to Compact.
  3. U2: open Work Orders twice; switch to Tech View. Set density to Comfortable.
  4. U3: open Work Orders once and stay on List.
  5. U4: open Work Orders once and switch to Tech View. Leave density as it is (Regular).
  6. Work out the weekly figures from your notes, counting each user (uid) once: for each display (list, tech_view, board_view), how many different uids have a work_orders_display_view event for it; and, among the users who used Tech View or Board View, how many have each density.
case.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Weekly display usage by distinct users: List 4 (every user opened the page on List first), Tech View 2 (U2, U4), Board View 1 (U1). U1's five visits count as 1 user.
  • Density spread across users who used Tech View or Board View: Compact 1 (U1), Comfortable 1 (U2), Regular 1 (U4), so 1 ÷ 3 = 33.3% each. No user appears twice and U3 (List only) is not in it.
  • Check the user totals add up: 1 + 1 + 1 = 3 users in the density figures, and 4 different uids in all.
  • The report page itself is built by the report owner inside Google Analytics, outside ShopView, and is not part of this test (QA lead's ruling below).

Source — where this behaviour comes from

  • Epic SV-10043; story SV-10593 (Story 12, Google Analytics for display and field usage); PRD Confluence 845185030, edited 7 Oct 2026 (status line "PRD v33"), S12-R4, S12-R11, S12-R13, read 8 Oct 2026. Event names and timing: SV-10593 comments by Slavcho Mitrov and Milos Vasic, 6 Oct 2026 (the agreed GA4 event table); earlier event contract on Review Decisions page 853901313 (29 Sep 2026) uses older names.
  • QA lead's ruling, 12 Oct 2026 17:22 UTC, in the QA session chat, after he asked for these checks to be tested on the ShopView QA branch. Question put to him: “How should I record the analytics tests, now that everything ShopView sends checks out on the QA branch?” His answer, word for word: “Pass on QA-branch data (Recommended)”. The steps were changed on 12 Oct 2026 under Rule 114(d) to read the events in the browser and work the figures out with the PRD's own rules, instead of opening the Google Analytics report.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S12-R4: “Report weekly display usage by distinct users.”
  • S12-R11: “Report density distribution.”
  • S12-R13: “Do not count repeated events from one user as additional users.”
